History: #955 (LEGION-11) was OPEN at implementation start, so per the plan's Case B the branch was first built on a `jj duplicate` of #955's single fix commit (993e41e66622). The pr-queue organizer then reported #955 not ready (back in testing) and asked for #980 to land independently as T0; the architect chose to drop the duplicate. `jj rebase -s <task 1> -d <plan handoff>` produced exactly the predicted index.ts placement conflict in tasks 4 and 6; both were resolved toward main's placement: `reconnectWorkers`/`pruneSecretFiles` and the pending-controller-notice block stay before the API as on main (item 4 remains LEGION-11's; #955 rebases over this restructure), and only the rename comment (`enableLaunches()`), the launch hold, `stop()` hoisting, and the post-hold release sequence are this branch's. Two imports LEGION-11's commit had added to index.test.ts (`spyOn`, `type DaemonStateResponse`) were re-added in the task 3 and task 6 commits. LEGION-11's own test left with the duplicate. The chain is main -> plan handoff 014c528d -> the eight LEGION-28 commits -> implement handoff.

commitsPerTask.message: feat(daemon): the command runner takes a per-call timeout and reports a kill as a timeout
feat(daemon): slow_command_timeout_seconds budgets boot probes and workspace provisioning
fix(daemon): a boot probe killed at its budget is retried with capped exponential backoff, never a crash loop
feat(daemon): a launch hold queues every spawn until boot releases it
fix(daemon): one worker's reconnect failure no longer aborts every other worker's reconnect
fix(daemon): boot serves state and the API while the OMP probe retries; no pane launches until it passes
fix(workspace): provisioning commands get the slow budget, a killed command is reported as a timeout, and a clone lands only when complete
docs(daemon): boot probe retry, launch hold, per-claim reconnect isolation, slow_command_timeout_seconds, clone-into-temp

config.test.ts: slowCommandTimeoutSeconds YAML beats env beats the 300 default; non-positive values refuse startup naming the key
cli/__tests__/index.test.ts: legion probe-image gives up after the bounded retry (sleeps [10000,20000,40000,80000,160000], 6 attempts) when every attempt times out

daemon/__tests__/index.test.ts: binds the API and loads state while the OMP probe is still timing out, launches nothing during the hold, and promotes the queued root and worker once it passes (acceptance 1); keeps retrying a runner-killed probe past the old bound with backoff capped at 300 s; definitive pi.agents / plugin-load / launch-prefix refusals now assert state WAS loaded, NATS WAS opened and closed, and the instance lock released (acceptance 2); the old bounded five-attempt give-up sub-case was deleted

processes.test.ts: queues a root admitted and a worker spawned while launches are held, and launches both once enableLaunches() runs; holds a resurrection and a controller launch during the hold and replays both after enableLaunches(); a throw while reconnecting one worker claim is logged with its token and leaves that claim alone while the other two are reconciled (acceptance 3); a throw while re-arming one root's deadline is logged and the other roots are armed

workspace.test.ts: clone into a temporary sibling then rename into place with every command under the 300 s budget; a clone killed at its budget is reported as `Command timed out after 300 s (ran 300.4 s): jj git clone …`, leaves nothing at the final path, and the second attempt clones fresh (acceptance 6); an existing final dir without .jj is removed and re-cloned with a log; a plain non-timeout failure still reads `Command failed (exit 1): jj git fetch -R <dir>\nfatal: x`
trickyParts: The injected test `sleep` in index.test.ts is shared between the probe backoff and the ProcessManager's registration deadlines/boot watchdog; a sleep that resolves immediately fires the deadlines and retires the panes the test asserts on. The acceptance-1 test resolves only the probe's two backoffs and leaves later sleeps pending.

The launch hold's `ensureController()` gate must come after `cancelControllerRegistrationDeadline()` but before the spawn; the pending-controller-notice `ensureController` at boot now runs after the hold (it opens a pane).
`stop()` is hoisted above the hold and guards `lingerTimer !== undefined`; `lingerTimer` became a `let` assigned after the hold.

The two `WorkerAdmission` decisions (`launchOrQueue`, `resumeOrQueueExisting`) gate on `workerPromotionEnabled` in addition to the cap, exactly as the planner's verification 2 described; `promoteQueuedWorker`/`reconcileWorkerAdmission` were already gated.

`bunx biome check packages/` from the repo root cannot run in this repo: packages/claude-envoy-bridge/biome.json is a second root configuration (pre-existing); biome was run per affected package instead.
deviations: Task 3's commit also updates the two index.test.ts retry-policy tests the plan listed under task 6 ('retries a boot probe whose launch died transiently' -> sleeps [10000, 20000]; the bounded give-up sub-case replaced by the unbounded capped-backoff test), so that commit is self-consistent; task 6's commit carries only the ordering tests.

Task 4's commit also enables launches in processes.thermo-ops.test.ts's manager fixture (it models a booted daemon) and adds `await processManager.replayHeldRecoveries()` after boot admission in index.ts so the intermediate commit keeps the pending-notice controller spawn working; task 6 then moves that block after the hold.

workspace.test.ts 'repairs a stale reused workspace after its remote issue branch is deleted' got an explicit 60 s test timeout: it runs ~30 real jj subprocesses (one variant through mise) and exceeded bun's 5 s default on this host (load average 80–96 during implementation); packages/workspace is not run by CI (pr-and-main.yaml runs only packages/daemon).
The plan's task 7 said `commandTimeoutMs: 300_000` on every workspace test; the two real-jj tests also got it (they ignore it) so the deps type stays uniform.
